name: Philippus de Harveng
evidence: Extensive searches for English translations of Philippus de Harveng and his known works (Responsio de damnatione Salomonis, Life of Augustine of Hippo, Commentaria in Cantica canticorum) found no English translations. Works appear only in Latin editions.

name: Atto Vercellensis
evidence: Searched for translations of Atto Vercellensis, his Polypticum, De pressuris ecclesiasticis, and biblical commentaries. Found references to Latin editions and scholarly works in English about his writings, but no complete English translations of his works.

name: Bruno Herbipolensis
evidence: Searched for English translations of Bruno Herbipolensis (Bruno of Würzburg) and his Psalterium beati Brunonis episcopi herbipolensis. Found only Latin editions (Koberger printed editions 1494-1497) and manuscript references. No English translation located.

name: Landulfus Sagax
evidence: Searched Historia Miscella and Historia Romana by Landulfus Sagax. Found Latin editions and an Italian translation, but no English translation despite being a significant medieval historical work. Available in Latin scholarly editions and Internet Archive.

name: Ado Viennensis
evidence: Searched for English translations of Ado Viennensis, his Chronicon (Breviarium chronicorum), and Martyrologium. Found Latin manuscripts and editions but no English translation despite the work's significance in medieval historiography.

name: Ernaldus Bonaevallis
evidence: Searched for English translations of Ernaldus Bonaevallis (Arnold of Bonneval), his De ultimis verbis domini and De septem verbis Domini in cruce. Found scholarly references to the Latin text but no published English translation.

name: Bernaldus Constantiensis
evidence: Searched for English translations of Bernold of Constance and his works. Found Latin editions and scholarly references but no evidence of comprehensive English translations of his corpus.

name: Goffridus Vindocinensis
evidence: Searched for English translations of Geoffrey of Vendôme (Goffridus Vindocinensis) and his sermons, hymns, and theological tracts. Found that best edition is Sirmond edition (Paris, 1610) in Latin, no English translations located.

name: Oddo Astensis
evidence: Searched for English translations of Oddo (Odo) Astensis and his Expositio in Psalmos. Found references in Migne's Patrologia Latina (volumes 164-165), Gallica, and manuscript repositories, but no English translation.

name: Arnulfus Lexoviensis
evidence: Searched for English translations of Arnulf of Lisieux (Arnulfus Lexoviensis) and his ecclesiastical letters. Found that letters were edited by Frank Barlow and published by Royal Historical Society (1939) but these appear to be scholarly editions in Latin/English analysis rather than complete translations.

name: Marianus Scottus
evidence: Searched for English translations of Marianus Scottus and his Chronicon Scotorum. While the chronicle was influential in medieval England (used by Florence of Worcester and John of Worcester), the Chronicle itself was never formally translated to English. Only Florence of Worcester's separate chronicle (which used Marianus as basis) was translated by Thomas Forester (1854).

name: Landulfus Mediolanensis
evidence: Searched for English translations of Landulf of Milan and his Historia Mediolanensis. Found Italian translation by Alessandro Visconti and Latin scholarly editions, but no English translation.

name: Claudius Taurinensis
evidence: Found multiple English translations: (1) Commentary on Philemon - English translation available at https://blog.undustedtexts.com/2024/10/claudius-of-turin-commentary-on-philemon.html and Academia.edu; (2) Commentary on Galatians and Defense/Reply to Abbot Theodemir translated by Allen Cabaniss in Library of Christian Classics (Early Medieval Theology, Vol. IX).

name: Hericus Antissiodorensis
evidence: Hericus Antissiodorensis is identified with Haimo (Haymo) of Auxerre. Multiple English translations found: (1) Commentary on the Epistles of Saint Paul - Part I: Romans (Brepols, 2026, translator Benjamin Wheaton); (2) Commentary on the Book of Jonah (translated by Deborah Everhart, Cistercian Publications); (3) Commentary on Second Thessalonians (Medieval Institute Publications TEAMS series).

name: Wandalbertus Prumiensis
evidence: Searched for English translations of Wandalbert of Prüm, his verse martyrology (c. 848), Life of St. Goar, and supplementary poems. Found facsimile and Latin manuscript information but no English translation.

name: Egbertus Eboracensis
evidence: Searched for English translations of Egbert of York (Egbertus Eboracensis) and his works, particularly the Paenitentiale Ecgberhti (Ecgberhtine penitential). Found scholarly references and manuscript editions but no published English translation.

name: Folcardus Sithivensis
evidence: Searched for English translations of Folcardus Sithivensis (hagiographer fl. 1080) and his Miracula Sancti Bertini. Found Latin text in Documenta Catholica Omnia but no English translation.

name: Lupus de Olmeto
evidence: Searched for English translations of Lupus de Olmeto and his Regula monachorum ex scriptis Hieronymi collecta (15th c.). Found references to manuscripts at Bodleian and BnF, and an Italian translation (by Mattheo da Ferrara), but no English translation.

name: Adrianus II
evidence: Searched for English translations of Pope Adrian II (792-872) and his diplomatic/papal correspondence. Found biographical and historical references but no specific English translation of his correspondence or works.
